column1: # FIPS foreign-failure baseline (Company Agent ruling 125, rulings.md 9589c37).
# The FIPS job's (ci.yml and nightly.yml `fips`, both `make test-fips`)
# counterpart of foreign-failures.tsv, kept in its own file with its own row
# format: scripts/foreignfailures -job fips reads only this file and only kind
# panic rows, and the Integration job's reader refuses both, so a FIPS row can
# never excuse an Integration failure, nor the reverse.
# Under GODEBUG=fips140=only the Go runtime enforces by PANIC. A panic is
# foreign only when ALL of these hold, and otherwise it still gates:
#   - the panicking test is exactly a row's package and top-level test name
#     (no wildcards, no subtests: a panic kills the whole binary);
#   - every `panic:` line's message is exactly the row's message;
#   - the panicking goroutine's stack passes through the row's frame, and
#     through the listed test function itself;
#   - that test is the package's only failure, and no other package, build
#     or run fails (a plain failure of a listed test gates too: kind panic is
#     the only kind).
# The panic killed the test binary, so every test after it never ran. For
# each attributed package the checker therefore runs ALL of its other
# top-level tests again, by explicit name (`go test -list`, then `-run
# '^(A|B|...)$'`, split into batches whose pattern stays under 64 KiB, the
# exec argument limit; no -skip, no -short, no build tag), under the same
# GOFIPS140/fips140=only environment and derived build tags, and the job
# passes only when that rerun passes and runs every name. Names `make test`'s
# TEST_SKIP drops are left out of the rerun exactly as they were from the run.
# A rerun repeats: when a round fails only by another listed test's panic
# that meets every rule above, the next round excludes that test too, with
# the same guards. The rounds are bounded by the package's number of rows
# (one per test it can exclude); a round past the bound gates, as does any
# other round failure. Every round is printed as a `rerun:` line.
# Only ruling-104 foreign classes may be listed. upstream is the open issue,
# repo#number (several joined by +); closing_release is the release whose
# adoption fixes it. A row is removed in the PR that adopts its closing
# release. frame is a Go function as a stack trace names it, without its
# arguments; message is the panic's text, last because it holds spaces.
# docs/test/integration.md describes both baselines.
# kind
panic
